Extract a simulated dataset or surface

Source: R/simulation.R
simulated_data.Rd

Extract a simulated dataset or surface

Usage

simulated_data(object, simulation = 1)

simulated_surface(object, simulation = 1)

Arguments

object

Output from simulate_glgpm().

simulation

A single simulation number, defaulting to one. These accessors return one sf object at a time; use simulated_values() to extract multiple simulations in one tidy table.

Value

simulated_data() returns the sample sf data with its response column replaced by the selected simulation, ready for refitting. simulated_surface() returns the grid sf data with columns for the spatial effect, nugget, group effect, linear predictor and mean, with class RiskMap_simulated_surface so that it can be mapped with plot().

Examples

library(sf)
locations <- st_as_sf(data.frame(x = c(0, 1000, 2000), y = 0),
                      coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32629)

grid <- st_as_sf(data.frame(x = c(500, 1500), y = 500),
                 coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32629)

model <- specify_glgpm(response ~ gp(),
                       data = locations,
                       family = "gaussian",
                       parameters = list(beta = 1,
                                         sigma2 = 1,
                                         phi = 2,
                                         sigma2_me = 0.1))

sim <- simulate_glgpm(model,
                      nsim = 2,
                      what = c("data", "surface"),
                      prediction_grid = grid,
                      seed = 1)

simulated_data(sim, simulation = 1)
#> Simple feature collection with 3 features and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 2000 ymax: 0
#> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / UTM zone 29N
#>         geometry     response
#> 1    POINT (0 0)  0.851613371
#> 2 POINT (1000 0)  0.889323292
#> 3 POINT (2000 0) -0.002729952
